**6B.6 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**
Overall: **mostly no / mixed**

**Positive / partial**
- **World Bank helps Bangladesh provide basic services, opportunities, and build resilience for displaced Rohingya and host communities** | World Bank | 2024-05-28 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co | Claim: Bangladesh and partners funded health, nutrition, education, water, shelters, livelihood support, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This is the strongest positive evidence that the state helped reduce suffering in a long-running displacement crisis, though it was heavily partner-financed and not clearly a Hasina-led crisis-response success. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`

- **UN and partners seek $852.4M to support Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi hosts** | UNHCR / UN in Bangladesh | 2024-03-13 | https://www.unhcr.org/news/press-releases/un-and-partners-seek-852-4m-support-rohingya-refugees-and-bangladeshi-hosts | Claim: The 2024 Rohingya response plan, under Bangladeshi authorities, aimed to provide food, shelter, health care, protection, education, and livelihood support, especially for women and children. Positive, but it is humanitarian coordination rather than clear proof that Hasina personally reduced suffering better during crises. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **UNICEF and Japan join hands to improve the well-being of Bangladeshi and Rohingya children living** | United Nations in Bangladesh | 2024-03-03 | https://bangladesh.un.org/en/262180-unicef-and-japan-join-hands-improve-the-well-being-of-bangladeshi-and-rohingya-children-living | Claim: UNICEF reported expanded services for Rohingya children, women, and host communities in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char, including education, WASH, health, and nutrition. This is real suffering-reduction in a crisis setting, but it is partner-led and narrow rather than broad national crisis management. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **WHO Bangladesh celebrates landmark success of the Health and Gender Support Project in Cox’s Bazar** | WHO Bangladesh | 2024-06-22 | https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/22-06-2024-who-bangladesh-celebrates-landmark-success-of-the-health-and-gender-support-project-in-cox-s-bazar | Claim: The project, run through the Ministry of Health and World Bank funding, produced quantified service-delivery gains such as screenings, trained health workers, and expanded disease-surveillance capacity. This is concrete evidence of measured crisis-response delivery in a highly vulnerable area. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **UNFPA Bangladesh annual report 2024** | UNFPA Bangladesh | 2024 | https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024 | Claim: UNFPA reported targeted services for women, girls, adolescents, persons with disabilities, and disaster-affected areas, including emergency reproductive health, GBV services, and cash assistance after floods and Cyclone Remal. This is the best direct positive evidence for reducing avoidable suffering during natural-disaster shocks, though it is still largely partner-led. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Negative**
- **Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards** | UN OHCHR | 2024-07-26 | https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights | Claim: The UN said more than 170 people had been killed, warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity, and said some injured people were denied medical care. This is very strong evidence that the state failed to reduce avoidable suffering during the July crisis. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | Reuters | 2024-07-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153 | Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed opponents instead of pivoting to visible harm reduction or accountability. This is strong evidence against transparent, civilian-protective crisis management. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral** | Reuters | 2024-07-20 | https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/ | Claim: Reuters described a nationwide curfew, internet/text shutdowns, and army deployment as violence escalated. That is evidence of coercive control and information suppression, not a strategy focused on minimizing civilian harm. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **Bangladesh back UN investigation into grave abuses** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-26 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses | Claim: HRW said the crackdown was the deadliest in Bangladesh’s recent history, with at least 440 killed. This is strong evidence that the state response amplified suffering rather than reducing it. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **Fears grip ethnic minorities after deadly violence in Bangladesh** | Reuters | 2024-09-21 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/fears-grip-ethnic-minorities-after-deadly-violence-in-bangladesh-3626672 | Claim: Ethnic minorities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts were living in fear after clashes, with homes and businesses burned and families displaced despite heavy patrols. This indicates that vulnerable groups in a poor region were not effectively protected from avoidable suffering. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.3`, `6B.2`

- **Bangladesh's economy bogged down by high unemployment, inflation** | Reuters | 2024-08-08 | https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1 | Claim: Reuters summarized widening external deficits, taka depreciation, falling reserves, IMF dependence, and stagnant job creation. This is negative evidence that Hasina did not prevent avoidable economic suffering in 2024. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

- **Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024** | World Bank | 2024-10-01 | https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672 | Claim: The Bank projected rising extreme poverty and more than one Gini-point higher inequality, with jobs still weak. That undercuts any claim that the government broadly reduced avoidable suffering from the economic shock. | IDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`

**Search gap**
- I found credible evidence of **targeted humanitarian relief** for Rohingya, disaster-affected women, and children.
- I did **not** find strong evidence that Hasina’s own government proactively and transparently reduced civilian suffering during the year’s biggest crises, especially the July crackdown.
- The positive items are mostly **partner-led crisis aid** or **narrow sector programs**; the negative items are broader and more directly tied to the state’s 2024 crisis response.
